extracted.intended_audience: progressive reformers, policymakers, public intellectuals, and educated general readers
extracted.subtask_description: Normative criteria and policy principles for reshaping economic, educational, and industrial institutions so as to foster genuine individuality, intellectual independence, and democratic fulfillment rather than mere money-making. Emphasizes how state action, education, and reorganization of economic incentives can align private fulfillment with public service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individuality requires pursuit of a disinterested object
rubrics_metrics.description: The truth is that individuality cannot be dissociated from the pursuit of a disinterested object. It is a moral and intellectual quality, and it must be realized by moral and intellectual means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A man's individuality is shown by zeal and skill in pursuing an exclusive interest (e.g., painting, running a railroad) pursued single‑mindedly and disinterestedly. Individuality is projected into excellent work; excellence of work reunites the individual with society and has unequivocal social value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic systems should promote special purposes, not mere money‑making
rubrics_metrics.description: An economic system that asks only that every man make as much money as he can tends to produce individuals distinguishable only by quantity of success, not by special purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genuine individuality is promoted when people are divided by special purposes and reunited by excellence in those purposes. Systems that reward only enterprise in money-making stifle true individuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward structures should align with excellence of work; eliminate 'easy money' opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: The system which most encourages mere cupidity is one which affords too many opportunities for making 'easy money' (e.g., profits from mines, urban real estate, municipal franchises, semi‑monopolies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminating opportunities to accumulate unearned wealth will bring rewards closer to the quality of work; otherwise mercenary motives will compel mediocrity and reduce the number of individuals who pursue excellence for its own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize industry for public benefit to strengthen correspondence of quality and reward
rubrics_metrics.description: So far as industry is organized under national control for the public benefit, there would be a much closer correspondence between the quality of the work and the amount of the reward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well‑managed corporation or national organization can promote promotion and reward based on demonstrated ability and good work; technical standards, trades, professions, and craft traditions help maintain high standards by providing reputational and disciplinary incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust compensation to human needs to enable disinterested work
rubrics_metrics.description: The only way in which work can be made entirely disinterested is to adjust its compensation to the needs of a normal and wholesome human life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If compensation meets normal human needs, individuals can pursue excellence without being driven purely by pay. (The text notes tensions and practical difficulties in fully accomplishing this—equitable adjustment strictly by earnings may be impossible or undesirable in some respects.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Diminish undesirable competition; encourage competition for quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The state can diminish undesirable competition and encourage the desirable competition in which men compete chiefly to excel in the quality of their work rather than for money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies should reduce mercenary incentives and promote competing to meet technical and professional standards; desirable competition is among craftsmen, professionals, scientists, etc., where tradition and honor keep standards high.

rubrics_metrics.name: National education must arouse intellectual conscience and uproot national irresponsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: American public opinion must be moved from acceptance of national irresponsibility to an understanding of how national education can promote individual emancipation and growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education should expose and uproot intellectual insincerity and the tradition of evading collective responsibilities. Critics and educators should be uncompromising in advancing revolutionary ideas to displace traditional error and stimulate public acceptance of constructive national programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual freedom requires material resources, discipline, and an audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom of speech alone is insufficient; in the absence of adequate material, discipline, and audience, words and thoughts are without avail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To cultivate genuine intellectual independence provide the material conditions (time, livelihood), disciplinary training (technical standards, craft/profession norms), and public forums/audiences so ideas can be developed, tested, and influential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transform private interests into service to the nation to harmonize private and public goods
rubrics_metrics.description: In a complete democracy a man must in some way be made to serve the nation in the very act of contributing to his own individual fulfillment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional design should systematically convert private pursuits into contributions to public welfare so that individuals realize fulfillment through serving fellow‑men rather than sacrificing private ends repeatedly for public good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase labor independence and reduce class grievances via national policy
rubrics_metrics.description: State policies should stimulate labor to more efficiency, diminish grievances, lend assistance to raise standards of living, and restrict the demoralizing effect of competition among laborers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By promoting labor's economic independence and addressing class grievances, national policy makes the average workingman more of an individual and increases opportunities to redeem individual interest by excellence of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform must be systematic, phased, and realistic while critics remain uncompromising in theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Sudden, drastic substitution of national regulation for the existing system would be disastrous; admissions of practical limits do not justify abandoning systematic policy toward individual and national amelioration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate radical theory uncompromisingly in critique, but pursue practical, realistic, and incremental policies for implementation; expect unforeseen measures to be necessary as reforms proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual emancipation demands disciplined assertion rather than mere contrarianism
rubrics_metrics.description: Past American heresies often failed because they lacked an authentic intellectual discipline and sought merely to be different rather than to develop a disciplined, constructive alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assertive critics should ground their agitation in disciplined ideas connected to a constructive national programme; mere negative or anti‑national protests that lack disciplined methods and organization are likely to be sterile.
